statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-82209: with libpsl support enabled, libcurl does not make a cookie host-only when its Domain attribute names an origin host that is itself a public suffix (for example Domain=co.uk set by co.uk), and instead stores it for the whole suffix, so it is sent to unrelated sibling hosts such as attacker.co.uk (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-82209.html). curl lists it as affecting releases from 7.46.0, with 8.17.0 through 8.21.0 affected on the current release line, and fixed it in curl 8.22.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/95c1e8915dce64606bd753fd47fc0bd236e31cd6, which is in the curl-8_22_0 release tag and not in curl-8_21_0. Alpine also lists it as fixed in curl 8.22.0-r0 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-82209). The DHI Alpine curl package is built from Alpine's aports curl recipe at the upstream curl release, and its build definition carries no patch for this CVE. The DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 (in both the main and the security repository), 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, on x86_64 and aarch64, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. None of the builds before 8.22.0-r0 is based on curl 8.22.0 or later, so 8.22.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.22.0, is the first fixed build. Every published DHI Alpine curl build links libpsl (libpsl.so.5 in libcurl's NEEDED list), so the affected PSL check is built in.
